newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends firmer, but off highs.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends firmer, but off highs.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures scored moderate gains on Monday, boosted by mixed trade buying and speculative short covering, but producer-led selling capped the day's gains, market sources said.
March futures gained 2.35 cents per lb, to close at 105.60, having traded from 103.70 to 107.20. May climbed 2.20, to 103.35, while spot December rose 1.35 to 113.10.

Arabica prices rose in an early round of trade and speculative interest, but was met with steady origin selling near 105 cents basis March. The buying resumed at midsession, however, aided by open interest data showing a sharp increase in open positions overnight.

On the leading March contract, open interest jumped 1,196 lots at last Friday's close, to a total of 15,321 lots. Most of the increase was thought to have come from a new round of speculative shorts, dealers said.

March delivery managed to clear a key nearby hurdle at 105.70 cents, advancing to 107.20, its highest price in four sessions. But expectations for a modest build in the CSCE's certified cache kept the upside in check, traders said.

After the close of trading, the CSCE reported gradable stocks grew by 2,000 60-kg bags for the week ended December 6, to 2,321 bags. In addition, another 5,500 bags were certified for delivery sometime between December 6-9, and a further 11,750 bags were reported pending grading in Miami warehouses.

Traders said that while the stock figures contained few surprises, the increase, the first in months, served to remind market operators that supply flows from Latin America were on the increase. The build also reflects a rush by suppliers to capitalize on spot December's steep premium before the contract expires.

"Most people realized there is a rush to get some coffee to the board for December to take advantage of it," said one trader. "More will come in, but we're not talking about major quantities," he added.
Technically, resistance was seen at 107.50 cents, 0.30 cent above today's high. Sell stops were believed well-placed under 102.00 cents, and then toward 100.00 cents ($1).
An estimated 9,786 lots changed hands on Monday.
-- Wendy Pollack, New York Commodities Desk +1 212 859 1640
